title: feedback-carton-quickpatch-priorities-sep-2026
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a compact synthesis of customer signals gathered between 2026-08-01 and 2026-08-28 (inbound tickets, CSM calls, onboarding notes, and a handful of in-product surveys). Goal: surface high-leverage quickpatches (<=2 weeks eng effort) and a prioritized set of feature asks that should inform next sprint conversation with product and serving-runtime.

Topline takeaway (tl;dr):
- Two priority classes: 1) small runtime/ops friction patches (KV-cache visibility, transient latency spikes, error message clarity) that unblock many customers and have low implementation cost; 2) higher-impact feature asks (dedicated autoscale observability, model-variant rollout controls, prompt-template snapshotting) that require product/UX scoping and medium effort.
- Rough signal magnitude: ~18 distinct customers raised one or more items that map to the quickpatch list; an additional ~12 raised medium-impact asks. A small subset (4 customers) reported production incidents tied to the same root cause (cache eviction behavior + ambiguous fallback).

Raw customer snippets (anonymized):
- "We saw a 3–5x token cost bump when requests hit the fallback chain mid-day — no visibility into why it fell back or which model served it." — fintech-analytics-startup
- "Our on-prem deployment occasionally returns a soft-503 and the console shows zero clues — had to rollback feature on our side." — healthcare-vertical customer
- "KV cache miss patterns are killing our latency p99s; we need metrics and a way to pin prefixes." — marketplace platform

Signal breakdown (themes):
1) KV-cache visibility & controls (high frequency, low-medium effort)
   - Symptoms: unexpected cache evictions, no per-key metric, opaque behavior during instance restarts.
   - Impact: increased cost (more tokens regenerated), p99 latency regressions, customer confusion.
   - Suggested quickpatches: expose per-tenant cache hit/miss counters in Console, add a "pin prefix" toggle in the deployment config (experimental).
   - Customer asks: exportable CSV of cache activity, alert when hit-rate drops below threshold.

2) Transparent fallbacks & model-routing explanations (medium frequency, medium effort)
   - Symptoms: fallbacks trigger without context (cost tier vs capacity), customers can't map requests to actual model variant used.
   - Impact: billing disputes, trust erosion, inability to debug quality/regression.
   - Suggested quickpatch: add a response-level header/field "served_model_variant" and a runtime reason code (e.g., capacity_fallback, policy_route, region_failover).

3) Latency spike surface and auto mitigation (p99 spikes observed by multiple customers)
   - Symptoms: periodic p99 spikes aligned to autoscale events or full-GPU packing changes.
   - Impact: user-facing timeouts; for chat apps this leads to degraded UX.
   - Suggested quickpatch: console timeline overlay showing recent scaling and packing events; short-term throttling knob per route.

4) Error clarity and retry semantics (low effort, high customer frustration)
   - Symptoms: soft 503/502/timeout with opaque text. Customers unsure whether to retry or back off.
   - Suggested quickpatch: standardize error responses with explicit retryable: true/false and suggested backoff window.

5) Dedicated capacity observability (lower frequency but high impact)
   - Asks: per-pool SLA metering, commit utilization trends, runway forecasting for reserved capacity.
   - This is medium-term but repeatedly cited by customers negotiating renewal/contracts.

Prioritized quickpatch backlog (recommended ordering):
A. Add "served_model_variant" header + reason code to API responses (owner: serving-runtime; est effort: 1 week): high impact for debugging/billing disputes.
B. Expose KV-cache hit/miss counters and simple CSV export in Console (owner: observability + serving-runtime; est effort: 1.5 weeks): direct ROI via fewer tickets and cost reductions for customers.
C. Standardize error payloads with retryable flag and suggested backoff (owner: api-surface + sdk; est effort: 3 days): reduces churn and confusion.
D. Console overlay for recent autoscale/packing events per deployment (owner: console; est effort: 1 week): helps correlate spikes to infra actions.
E. Short-term per-route throttling toggle (owner: runtime + console; est effort: 1 week): immediate mitigation for noisy routes.

Medium-term feature asks (for product scoping):
- Dedicate pool utilization forecasting & commitment runway (product + finance): customers want to see if they are under/overprovisioned before renewal.
- Model-variant canary & rollback UI (product + console + runtime): allow pinning percent traffic to new model, automatic rollback on eval regressions.
- Prompt-template snapshotting and version diffing (product + devex): many customers managing templates ask for in-platform versioning and dry-run evaluation.

Risk flags and open questions:
- Adding response-level served_model_variant header may expose internal naming; need security/contract review for PII or internal model IDs. Propose mapping to public-friendly variant labels.
- Pinning prefixes in KV-cache: how to surface limits and cross-tenant memory impact? SRE input required.
- Some quickpatches touch billing (served_model_variant affects billing disputes). Finance should be looped in before rolling to GA.

Low-cost experiments to validate impact:
- A/B release of CSV cache export to 5 customers and measure ticket rate over 30 days.
- Flagrant-mode error payloads to a single environment for a subset of customers (opt-in) and monitor reduction in retry-related tickets.

Metrics to track post-change (suggested dashboards):
- "cache_hit_rate_by_tenant" daily trend + alerts if drop >10%
- "tickets_per_customer_week" (subset flagged KV-cache or fallback) pre/post quickpatch
- p99 latency by deployment over 7/30/90 days with overlay of scaling events

Owner/stake allocation recommendation:
- Fast-track (A-C): assign small cross-functional pod: 1 runtime engineer (Ethan P.), 1 console engineer (Sofia A.), 1 observability engineer (Diego M.), product lead (Maya C. as preparer).
- Medium-term: product-led scoping doc, include commercial (renewal) rep for dedicated pool features.

Communication plan (for customers):
- For each quickpatch we plan a short release note and a CS small-batch rollout. Suggested cadence: ship small fixes weekly and email/update affected customers within 48hrs of rollout.
- For medium features, schedule joint discovery calls with top-6 affected customers and surface roadmap timeline during Q4 renewal conversations.

Notes to self / unresolved items: 
- Confirm SRE constraints on adding pin-prefix to KV-cache (ticketing SRE before design doc).
- Decide canonical label set for served_model_variant (avoid exposing internal model hashes).
- Estimate billing implications for exposing fallback reason (compute cost vs. revenue disputes).

Next steps (owner + due dates):
- Draft API response header proposal & security checklist (owner: Maya C., due 2026-09-06).
- Spike Console CSV export UX and quick mock (owner: Sofia A., due 2026-09-08).
- Quick internal demo: show p99 overlay + autoscale events to CS/Eng (owner: Diego M., demo week of 2026-09-13).

Appendix: sample error payload (proposal) to standardize across SDKs:
{
  "error": "service_unavailable",
  "retryable": "true",
  "recommended_backoff_s": 5,
  "support_hint": "contact CS with request id"
}

If you want this boiled down further for an exec note (1 paragraph + recommended asks to sales), I can produce a one-pager.

— Maya
